correctness.rationale: The final narrowed theorem quantifies a,b>=2 and every n>=1, with only ONE first-one-deletion/append iteration. For a periodic two-run factor the number of ordinary distinct length-n factors is min(n,a)+min(n,b). The tortoise map preserves the number of ones and sends the first two zero gaps z0,z1 to their sum while leaving later zero gaps fixed. Equal images of distinct factors with m>=2 ones force (z0,z1)=(a,0),(0,a), giving exactly the pair {0^a1^{n-a},10^a1^{n-a-1}} at n=a+2,...,a+b. With exactly one 1 the only distinct colliding factors are {0^{n-1}1,10^{n-1}} at n=2,...,a+1; zero-only factors cannot collide with positive-one factors. Thus one double fiber, no larger fiber, at every 2<=n<=p and none for n>=p+1. The explicit piecewise c(n) follows. Independent new standalone direct-deletion and zero-gap checker verified all exact pair identities and output counts in 7139 parameter-length tests. This does not prove the infinite theorem by itself; the all-(a,b,n) gap argument does.
